Choose the frame by timestamp

Use the timeline for a rough location or type seconds for a specific moment, such as 1.25. The decoder selects the last frame whose start time is at or before the time you entered. A video frame spans an interval, so the displayed frame time can be slightly earlier. Time starts at the first displayed frame of the main video track.

Use Last frame if you need the final still. The video duration usually marks the end of playback, while the last visible frame starts earlier. Check the reported frame time under the controls.

Check the saved PNG

  1. Confirm that the preview shows the moment you want. Change the time and extract again if needed.
  2. Save the PNG and open it to verify its dimensions. The preview fits the page. The download uses the decoded frame at its display dimensions, including supported orientation metadata.
  3. If you need movement, use the local video-to-GIF tool. To save only sound, use the audio extractor.

PNG preserves the exported frame without additional JPEG compression. The frame has already been decoded from the video, and the PNG does not preserve HDR mastering metadata or improve source quality.

Which videos can the browser decode?

Try MP4, WebM or MOV. The video codec inside the file determines whether it decodes on this device. If the file has no readable video track or its codec is unsupported, try a known H.264 MP4 or use a desktop editor capable of reading the source. Export works on the main video track.

The tool uses the site’s self-hosted Mediabunny decoder and canvas renderer. Your selected file and output data stay in this tab. The original file is left intact.
